# Tempo Flow — Backlog v2 (ticket standard v2)

Written 1 Nov 2026 · Branch `docs/source-2026-11-01` · Draft PR #1352 into `integration`.

This is the **v2** backlog: every Tempo Flow ticket written to
[`docs/backlog/TICKET-STANDARD.md`](./TICKET-STANDARD.md) (v2, 1 Nov 2026). It supersedes the earlier
thin-format rewrite (`docs/backlog/BACKLOG.md`, tickets TRW-1001…TRW-1232) and the plan
`docs/backlog/REWRITE-PLAN.md`, both marked superseded and kept for history.

The plan, inventory, chunk layout, conflict list and fold-in map live in
[`docs/backlog/REWRITE-PLAN-v2.md`](./REWRITE-PLAN-v2.md). This file holds the ticket text only.

## How to read a ticket
Every ticket carries: `ID`, `Title`, `Stage`, `Pass`, `Depends`, `Folds-in`, then the 11 `AGENTS.md`
fields (`FOR`, `WHEN`, `WHY`, `GOAL`, `SCOPE`, `MUTATES`, `STEPS`, `DONE`, `EVIDENCE`, `DO NOT`,
`REPORT`) plus `SPEC`, `TESTS` (Given/When/Then), `NUMBERS` (range + source, or `UNKNOWN`),
`GATES`, and `OPEN`. The authority for what each field must contain is `TICKET-STANDARD.md`.

Ticket IDs are `TFV2-0001` upward, one per screen / component / backend function-table-endpoint, in
build order. `Pass` 1 = clunky (every state works); `Pass` 2 = matches v3 tokens/motion exactly.

## Groundwork — test infrastructure and config lane (comes before Chunk 1)

These tickets come first in build order. TFV2-0000a…d are ordinary factory tickets. CFG tickets are
**config lane: Amit** (CONVENTIONS §18): schema, test config and CI changes that factory lanes may not
make. A build ticket that needs a CFG ticket lists it in `Depends`.

### TFV2-0000a — Convex test fake: signed-out ctx, `delete`, `replace`, `unique`, scheduler recorder
- **Stage:** A · **Pass:** 1 · **Depends:** none · **Folds-in:** none
- **FOR:** Tempo Flow (`Levidavidspublic/tempo-rhythm`); lane per `factory/SLOTS.md`.
- **WHEN:** first.
- **WHY:** CONVENTIONS §16 (every backend ticket tests the signed-out case and seeds rows through the fake ctx); TICKET-STANDARD "Backend tickets include unit tests for every error case". Today `makeFakeCtx` always returns an identity and has no `delete`, `replace`, `unique()` or `scheduler`, so those tests cannot be written.
- **GOAL:** `convex/lib/testFakeCtx.ts` also exports `makeSignedOutCtx`, and every fake ctx supports `db.delete`, `db.replace`, `.unique()` and a recording `scheduler.runAfter`, proven by its own test file.
- **SCOPE:** `convex/lib/testFakeCtx.ts` · test: `convex/lib/testFakeCtx.test.ts`.
- **MUTATES:** `convex/lib/testFakeCtx.ts` (edit, additive only) · `convex/lib/testFakeCtx.test.ts` (new).
- **STEPS:** 1) Code-map check: read `convex/lib/testFakeCtx.ts` (74 lines today: `makeFakeCtx(userId, extraUsers)` and `run`); confirm none of `makeSignedOutCtx`, `delete`, `replace`, `unique`, `scheduler` exists. 2) In `makeFakeCtx`, add to `db`: `delete: async (id: string) => { table(id.split(":")[0]).delete(id); }` and `replace: async (id: string, doc: Row) => { const t = table(id.split(":")[0]); const old = t.get(id); if (!old) throw new Error(\`replace on missing row ${id}\`); t.set(id, { _id: id, _creationTime: old._creationTime, ...doc }); }`. 3) In `builder`, add `unique: async () => { const out = sorted(); if (out.length > 1) throw new Error("unique() found more than one row"); return out[0] ?? null; }`. 4) Add to the returned object `scheduler: { calls, runAfter: async (delayMs: number, fn: unknown, args: unknown) => { calls.push({ delayMs, fn, args }); return \`scheduled:${calls.length}\`; } }` where `const calls: { delayMs: number; fn: unknown; args: unknown }[] = [];` is declared inside `makeFakeCtx`. 5) Export `export function makeSignedOutCtx() { return { ...makeFakeCtx("users:signed-out"), auth: { getUserIdentity: async () => null } } as any; }`. 6) Create `convex/lib/testFakeCtx.test.ts` with the 7 TESTS cases. 7) Run DONE, then `bun run test:unit` to show no existing test broke.
- **DONE:** `bun test convex/lib/testFakeCtx.test.ts` → `7 pass`, `0 fail`; `bun run test:unit` → `0 fail`.
- **EVIDENCE:** both summaries pasted into the PR.
- **DO NOT:** change the signature or behaviour of `makeFakeCtx`, `run`, `withIndex`, `order`, `collect`, `take`, `first`, `get`, `insert`, `patch`, `query` or `normalizeId`; edit any other test; touch `convex/schema.ts`, `convex/auth*`, `.github/**`, `.env*`.
- **REPORT:** `status / ticket: TFV2-0000a / evidence: <DONE output> / changed: convex/lib/testFakeCtx.ts, convex/lib/testFakeCtx.test.ts / unknowns / notes for ticket sync`.
- **SPEC:** Test-only module (never imported by app code). New and changed exports:
  ```ts
  export function makeFakeCtx(userId: string, extraUsers?: string[]): any; // unchanged signature; db gains delete/replace, builder gains unique, ctx gains scheduler
  export function makeSignedOutCtx(): any; // auth.getUserIdentity() resolves null; db works as in makeFakeCtx
  export const run: (fn: unknown, ctx: unknown, args: unknown) => unknown; // unchanged
  ```
  Errors thrown by the fake: `replace` on a missing id → `"replace on missing row <id>"`; `unique()` with more than one row → `"unique() found more than one row"`. No user-facing copy.
- **TESTS:**
  - Given `makeSignedOutCtx()` / When `ctx.auth.getUserIdentity()` runs / Then it resolves `null`.
  - Given `makeFakeCtx("users:1")` and an inserted `tasks` row / When `ctx.db.delete(id)` runs / Then `ctx.db.get(id)` resolves `null`.
  - Given an inserted row `{ title: "A", n: 1 }` / When `ctx.db.replace(id, { title: "B" })` runs / Then `ctx.db.get(id)` equals `{ _id: id, _creationTime: 0, title: "B" }` (field `n` is gone).
  - Given no row with id `"tasks:999"` / When `ctx.db.replace("tasks:999", {})` runs / Then it rejects with `"replace on missing row tasks:999"`.
  - Given exactly one `tasks` row with `userId: "users:1"` / When `ctx.db.query("tasks").withIndex("by_userId", (q) => q.eq("userId", "users:1")).unique()` runs / Then it resolves that row; and with zero matching rows it resolves `null`.
  - Given two matching rows / When `.unique()` runs / Then it rejects with `"unique() found more than one row"`.
  - Given `makeFakeCtx("users:1")` / When `ctx.scheduler.runAfter(0, "fnRef", { a: 1 })` runs twice / Then `ctx.scheduler.calls` has length 2, `calls[0]` equals `{ delayMs: 0, fn: "fnRef", args: { a: 1 } }`, and the second call resolves `"scheduled:2"`.
- **NUMBERS:** 7 of 7 test cases pass; existing unit suite stays at `0 fail` (exact). No latency number applies to a test fake.
- **GATES:** 1 Build/typecheck/lint · 2 own TESTS green · 3 NUMBERS in range · 4 Google style formatting/naming · 5 secret + forbidden-tech scan · 6 scope guard · 7 config guard · 8 never weaken/skip/lower/delete a check · 9 Jev judge (typesafe/jev-1.13): instruction-following, formatting, naming, clean code each >= 0.85; a massive violation fails · 10 Process check: REPORT lists every STEP and DONE item with evidence; a missing item fails.
- **OPEN:** none.

### TFV2-0000b — Playwright helpers `tests/e2e/helpers/harness.ts`
- **Stage:** A · **Pass:** 1 · **Depends:** none · **Folds-in:** none
- **FOR:** Tempo Flow (`Levidavidspublic/tempo-rhythm`); lane per `factory/SLOTS.md`.
- **WHEN:** first.
- **WHY:** CONVENTIONS §15 and §20 (every UI spec opens its harness or screen, checks RTL, target size, motion and vitals the same way); TICKET-STANDARD NUMBERS ("each number becomes a pass/fail check").
- **GOAL:** One helper module gives every UI spec the same viewports, URL builders, direction check, console-error tracker, target-size check, motion check and LCP/CLS measurement.
- **SCOPE:** `tests/e2e/helpers/harness.ts` · test: `tests/e2e/helpers.spec.ts`.
- **MUTATES:** `tests/e2e/helpers/harness.ts` (new) · `tests/e2e/helpers.spec.ts` (new).
- **STEPS:** 1) Code-map check: `ls tests/e2e` (no `helpers/` folder today). 2) Create `tests/e2e/helpers/harness.ts` exporting exactly the SPEC API. 3) Implement `harnessUrl`/`screenUrl` as pure string builders (query keys in the order `state`, `lang`, `theme`; omit keys whose value is undefined). 4) Implement `openHarness` as `page.goto(harnessUrl(id, opts))` then wait for `page.locator(\`[data-testid^="${id}-"]\`).first()` to be visible; `openScreen` as `page.goto(screenUrl(route, opts))` then `page.waitForLoadState("domcontentloaded")`. 5) Implement `expectDir`, `trackConsoleErrors` (records `console` messages of type `error` and every `pageerror` message), `expectTargetSize`, `expectMotionBudget` (parses comma lists of `s`/`ms`; after the reduced-motion pass calls `page.emulateMedia({ reducedMotion: null })`) and `measureVitals` (two `page.goto(url)` calls, then reads `largest-contentful-paint` and `layout-shift` entries with `buffered: true` PerformanceObservers inside `page.evaluate`, resolving after 1,000 ms). 6) Create `tests/e2e/helpers.spec.ts` with the 7 TESTS cases; cases 3–7 use `page.setContent(…)` so they need no route. 7) Run DONE.
- **DONE:** `CI=1 bunx playwright test tests/e2e/helpers.spec.ts --reporter=line` → `7 passed`, no failures.
- **EVIDENCE:** the Playwright summary pasted into the PR.
- **DO NOT:** edit `playwright.config.ts` or any existing spec; add a dependency; call Convex; touch `convex/**`, `.github/**`, `.env*`.
- **REPORT:** `status / ticket: TFV2-0000b / evidence: <DONE output> / changed: tests/e2e/helpers/harness.ts, tests/e2e/helpers.spec.ts / unknowns / notes for ticket sync`.
- **SPEC:** Test-only module. Exact API:
  ```ts
  import type { Page } from "@playwright/test";
  export const VIEWPORTS: { readonly mobile: { readonly width: 390; readonly height: 844 }; readonly desktop: { readonly width: 1280; readonly height: 800 } };
  export type HarnessLang = "en" | "he";
  export function harnessUrl(id: string, opts?: { lang?: HarnessLang; theme?: "light" | "dark" }): string; // "/e2e/components/<id>?lang=…&theme=…"
  export function screenUrl(route: string, opts: { state: string; lang?: HarnessLang }): string;     // "<route>?state=…&lang=…"
  export function openHarness(page: Page, id: string, opts?: { lang?: HarnessLang; theme?: "light" | "dark" }): Promise<void>;
  export function openScreen(page: Page, route: string, opts: { state: string; lang?: HarnessLang }): Promise<void>;
  export function expectDir(page: Page, lang: HarnessLang): Promise<void>;        // <html dir="rtl" lang="he"> or <html dir="ltr" lang="en">
  export function trackConsoleErrors(page: Page): string[];
  export function expectTargetSize(page: Page, selector: string): Promise<void>; // every visible button, a[href], input, select, textarea, [role=switch|checkbox|radio|tab|option|button] under selector ≥ 24×24
  export function expectMotionBudget(page: Page, selector: string): Promise<void>; // max transition/animation duration ≤ 0.25 s; ≤ 0.001 s under reduced motion (tempo.css sets 0.01ms)
  export function measureVitals(page: Page, url: string): Promise<{ lcpMs: number; cls: number }>;
  ```
  Failure messages (Playwright `expect` with a message): target size → `"target smaller than 24x24: <tag>#<index> <w>x<h>"`; motion → `"motion over 250ms: <tag> <duration>s"`; reduced motion → `"motion not removed under reduced motion: <tag>"`. No user-facing copy.
- **TESTS:**
  - Given `harnessUrl("scheduled-job-row", { lang: "he", theme: "dark" })` / Then it equals `"/e2e/components/scheduled-job-row?lang=he&theme=dark"`; and `harnessUrl("x")` equals `"/e2e/components/x"`.
  - Given `screenUrl("/modules", { state: "empty", lang: "en" })` / Then it equals `"/modules?state=empty&lang=en"`.
  - Given `page.setContent('<html dir="rtl" lang="he"><body></body></html>')` / When `expectDir(page, "he")` runs / Then it passes; and `expectDir(page, "en")` throws.
  - Given content with a `<button style="width:40px;height:40px">` / When `expectTargetSize(page, "body")` runs / Then it passes; given a `<button style="width:20px;height:20px;padding:0;border:0">` it throws with a message starting `"target smaller than 24x24"`.
  - Given a `<div style="transition: opacity 120ms">` plus `<style>@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { div { transition-duration: 0.01ms; } }</style>` / When `expectMotionBudget(page, "body")` runs / Then it passes; given `transition: opacity 400ms` it throws with a message starting `"motion over 250ms"`.
  - Given `trackConsoleErrors(page)` then `page.evaluate(() => console.error("boom"))` / Then the returned array equals `["boom"]`.
  - Given `page.setContent("<h1>Hi</h1>")` served through `page.route("http://helpers.test/", …)` / When `measureVitals(page, "http://helpers.test/")` runs / Then `lcpMs` is a finite number ≥ 0 and `cls` is a number ≥ 0.
- **NUMBERS:** 7 of 7 cases pass. The helper thresholds are the catalogue numbers: target ≥ 24×24 CSS px (WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8, https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/#target-size-minimum); motion ≤ 250 ms (DESIGN.md motion rule; CONVENTIONS §5).
- **GATES:** 1 Build/typecheck/lint · 2 own TESTS green · 3 NUMBERS in range · 4 Google style formatting/naming · 5 secret + forbidden-tech scan · 6 scope guard · 7 config guard · 8 never weaken/skip/lower/delete a check · 9 Jev judge (typesafe/jev-1.13): instruction-following, formatting, naming, clean code each >= 0.85; a massive violation fails · 10 Process check: REPORT lists every STEP and DONE item with evidence; a missing item fails.
- **OPEN:** none.

### TFV2-0000c — Web state forcing `apps/web/lib/e2e/e2eState.ts` + `useE2EState`
- **Stage:** A · **Pass:** 1 · **Depends:** none · **Folds-in:** none
- **FOR:** Tempo Flow (`Levidavidspublic/tempo-rhythm`); lane per `factory/SLOTS.md`.
- **WHEN:** first.
- **WHY:** CONVENTIONS §3 ("every state must be forceable"), §14 (screens render fixtures for `?state=` and never contact Convex in e2e).
- **GOAL:** Every web screen can read a forced `?state=` value that exists only in a non-production build with the E2E bypass on.
- **SCOPE:** `apps/web/lib/e2e/e2eState.ts` · `apps/web/lib/e2e/useE2EState.ts` · test: `apps/web/lib/e2e/e2eState.test.ts`.
- **MUTATES:** `apps/web/lib/e2e/e2eState.ts` (new) · `apps/web/lib/e2e/useE2EState.ts` (new) · `apps/web/lib/e2e/e2eState.test.ts` (new).
- **STEPS:** 1) Code-map check: `ls apps/web/lib/e2e` (absent today, or holds only `HarnessFrame.tsx` from TFV2-0023a; do not touch that file). 2) Create `e2eState.ts` with `E2E_STATE_PATTERN`, `parseE2EState`, `isE2EBypass` exactly as in SPEC (no React or Next imports). 3) Create `useE2EState.ts` starting with `"use client";`, importing `useSearchParams` from `next/navigation` and the two functions, exporting `useE2EState()`. 4) Create `e2eState.test.ts` with the 6 TESTS cases. 5) Run DONE.
- **DONE:** `bun test apps/web/lib/e2e/e2eState.test.ts` → `6 pass`, `0 fail`.
- **EVIDENCE:** the `bun test` summary pasted into the PR.
- **DO NOT:** read `?state=` anywhere in production code paths without `isE2EBypass`; edit `proxy.ts`, `e2eWiringRoutes.ts` or any screen; touch `convex/**`, `.github/**`, `.env*`.
- **REPORT:** `status / ticket: TFV2-0000c / evidence: <DONE output> / changed: <3 files> / unknowns / notes for ticket sync`.
- **SPEC:**
  ```ts
  // apps/web/lib/e2e/e2eState.ts
  export const E2E_STATE_PATTERN = /^[a-z][a-z-]{0,23}$/;
  export function parseE2EState(raw: string | null, bypass: boolean): string | null {
    return bypass && raw !== null && E2E_STATE_PATTERN.test(raw) ? raw : null;
  }
  export function isE2EBypass(env: { NODE_ENV?: string; NEXT_PUBLIC_TEMPO_E2E_AUTH_BYPASS?: string }): boolean {
    return env.NODE_ENV !== "production" && env.NEXT_PUBLIC_TEMPO_E2E_AUTH_BYPASS === "1";
  }
  // apps/web/lib/e2e/useE2EState.ts ("use client")
  export function useE2EState(): string | null {
    return parseE2EState(useSearchParams().get("state"), isE2EBypass({ NODE_ENV: process.env.NODE_ENV, NEXT_PUBLIC_TEMPO_E2E_AUTH_BYPASS: process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_TEMPO_E2E_AUTH_BYPASS }));
  }
  ```
  No user-facing copy, no errors thrown.
- **TESTS:**
  - Given `parseE2EState("empty", true)` / Then `"empty"`.
  - Given `parseE2EState("empty", false)` / Then `null`.
  - Given `parseE2EState(null, true)` / Then `null`.

- **Stage:** E · **Pass:** 1 · **Depends:** none · **Folds-in:** none
- **FOR:** Tempo Flow (`Levidavidspublic/tempo-rhythm`); area `mobile`; lane per `factory/SLOTS.md`.

- **GOAL:** Mobile code can read a forced `?state=` and decide the `(tempo)` gate through pure functions bun can test.
- **SCOPE:** `apps/mobile/lib/e2e/e2eState.ts` · `apps/mobile/lib/e2e/useE2EMobile.ts` · test: `tests/unit/mobile_e2e_state.test.ts`.
- **MUTATES:** the three files above (all new).
- **STEPS:** 1) Code-map check: `ls apps/mobile/lib` (no `e2e/` folder today); read `apps/mobile/app/(tempo)/_layout.tsx` lines 13–25 for the current redirect order (do not edit it). 2) Create `e2eState.ts` with `parseE2EMobileState`, `TempoGate` and `tempoGate` exactly as in SPEC, importing nothing from `react-native`, `expo-*` or `react`. 3) Create `useE2EMobile.ts` importing `useLocalSearchParams` from `expo-router` and exporting `useE2EMobile()`. 4) Create `tests/unit/mobile_e2e_state.test.ts` (mobile tests live in `tests/unit/mobile_*.test.ts`, the folder the unit suite runs) importing only `e2eState.ts`, with the 6 TESTS cases. 5) Run DONE.
- **DONE:** `bun test tests/unit/mobile_e2e_state.test.ts` → `6 pass`, `0 fail`.
- **EVIDENCE:** the `bun test` summary pasted into the PR.
- **DO NOT:** edit `apps/mobile/app/(tempo)/_layout.tsx` (CFG-032 does); import Expo or React Native into `e2eState.ts`; touch `convex/**`, `.github/**`, `.env*`.
- **REPORT:** `status / ticket: TFV2-0000d / evidence: <DONE output> / changed: <3 files> / unknowns / notes for ticket sync`.
- **SPEC:**
  ```ts
  // apps/mobile/lib/e2e/e2eState.ts
  const STATE_PATTERN = /^[a-z][a-z-]{0,23}$/;
  export function parseE2EMobileState(raw: string | null, enabled: boolean): string | null {
    return enabled && raw !== null && STATE_PATTERN.test(raw) ? raw : null;
  }
  export type TempoGate = "sign-in" | "onboarding" | "render";
  export function tempoGate(input: { isLoading: boolean; isAuthenticated: boolean; hasProfile: boolean; onboardedAt: number | undefined; e2e: boolean }): TempoGate {
    if (input.e2e) return "render";
    if (!input.isLoading && !input.isAuthenticated) return "sign-in";
    if (input.hasProfile && input.onboardedAt === undefined) return "onboarding";
    return "render";
  }
  // apps/mobile/lib/e2e/useE2EMobile.ts
  export function useE2EMobile(): string | null {
    const { state } = useLocalSearchParams<{ state?: string }>();
    return parseE2EMobileState(state ?? null, process.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_TEMPO_E2E === "1");
  }
  ```
  No user-facing copy.
- **TESTS:**
  - Given `parseE2EMobileState("offline", true)` / Then `"offline"`; and `parseE2EMobileState("offline", false)` / Then `null`.
  - Given `parseE2EMobileState("Bad!", true)` / Then `null`.
  - Given `tempoGate({ isLoading: false, isAuthenticated: false, hasProfile: false, onboardedAt: undefined, e2e: false })` / Then `"sign-in"`.
  - Given the same input with `e2e: true` / Then `"render"`.
  - Given `{ isLoading: false, isAuthenticated: true, hasProfile: true, onboardedAt: undefined, e2e: false }` / Then `"onboarding"`.
  - Given `{ isLoading: true, isAuthenticated: false, hasProfile: false, onboardedAt: undefined, e2e: false }` / Then `"render"` (matches today's layout: no redirect while loading).
- **NUMBERS:** 6 of 6 cases pass (exact). No UI number applies (no visible UI).

### CFG-032 — Mobile `(tempo)` gate: E2E signed-out render — config lane: Amit
- **Stage:** config · **Pass:** 1 · **Depends:** TFV2-0000d, CFG-031 · **Folds-in:** none
- **FOR:** Tempo Flow (`Levidavidspublic/tempo-rhythm`); config lane: Amit (auth-gate change, like the web bypass in `apps/web/proxy.ts`). Factory lanes never build this.
- **WHEN:** after TFV2-0000d, CFG-031.
- **WHY:** CONVENTIONS §15. `apps/mobile/app/(tempo)/_layout.tsx` redirects every signed-out visitor to `/(auth)/sign-in`, so mobile screen specs cannot open a screen. The web app solves this with a dev-only bypass; mobile needs the same, dev-only.
- **GOAL:** In a dev build with `EXPO_PUBLIC_TEMPO_E2E=1`, `(tempo)` routes render signed out; in every other build the gate behaves exactly as today.
- **SCOPE:** `apps/mobile/app/(tempo)/_layout.tsx` (edit) · test: `tests/e2e/mobile/tempo-gate.spec.ts`.
- **MUTATES:** `apps/mobile/app/(tempo)/_layout.tsx` (edit) · `tests/e2e/mobile/tempo-gate.spec.ts` (new) · mobile auth gate (dev + flag only).
- **STEPS:** 1) Code-map check: read `apps/mobile/app/(tempo)/_layout.tsx` lines 13–25 (two `<Redirect>` branches). 2) Import `tempoGate` from `@/lib/e2e/e2eState` (TFV2-0000d) — use the import alias the file already uses for `lib`. 3) Replace the two `if` branches with `const gate = tempoGate({ isLoading, isAuthenticated, hasProfile: profile !== undefined && profile !== null, onboardedAt: profile?.onboardedAt, e2e: __DEV__ && process.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_TEMPO_E2E === "1" }); if (gate === "sign-in") return <Redirect href="/(auth)/sign-in" />; if (gate === "onboarding") return <Redirect href="/(auth)/onboarding" />;`. 4) Create `tests/e2e/mobile/tempo-gate.spec.ts` with the 1 TESTS case. 5) Run DONE and `bun test tests/unit/mobile_e2e_state.test.ts`.
- **DONE:** `CI=1 bunx playwright test --config playwright.mobile.config.ts tests/e2e/mobile/tempo-gate.spec.ts --reporter=line` → `1 passed`; `bun test tests/unit/mobile_e2e_state.test.ts` → `0 fail`.
- **EVIDENCE:** both outputs pasted into the PR.
- **DO NOT:** change the sign-in or onboarding routes; read the flag without `__DEV__`; touch `convex/auth*`, `apps/web/proxy.ts`, `.github/**`, `.env*`.
- **REPORT:** `status / ticket: CFG-032 / evidence: <DONE output> / changed: <2 files> / unknowns / notes for ticket sync`.

### TFV2-0001 — Bounded list helper `convex/lib/bounded.ts`
- **Stage:** A · **Pass:** 1 · **Depends:** none · **Folds-in:** #1348 (TM-0032)
- **FOR:** Tempo Flow (`Levidavidspublic/tempo-rhythm`); pure-helper lane per `factory/SLOTS.md`.
- **WHEN:** first.
- **WHY:** PRD §4.11 F-130 (per-user isolation, bounded reads); REWRITE-PLAN-v2 §6 chunk 1 "bounded queries + resource quotas"; CONVENTIONS §16 "Limits: every list read is bounded (… or `boundedQuery` from TFV2-0001)", §7 H ("Bytes" = UTF-8 length).
- **GOAL:** `convex/lib/bounded.ts` exports `boundedQuery`, a pure function that keeps rows in order until a row-count or UTF-8 byte budget would be exceeded and reports `truncated`, proven by its own test file.
- **SCOPE:** `convex/lib/bounded.ts` · test: `convex/lib/bounded.test.ts`.
- **MUTATES:** `convex/lib/bounded.ts` (new) · `convex/lib/bounded.test.ts` (new). No table, route, env or schema change.
- **STEPS:**
  1. Code-map: `ls convex/lib | grep -i bounded` → no output (the helper does not exist today); `grep -rn "boundedQuery" convex apps packages` → no output (no caller to keep working).
  2. Create `convex/lib/bounded.ts` with exactly the SPEC exports and algorithm. No imports.
  3. Create `convex/lib/bounded.test.ts` (`import { describe, expect, test } from "bun:test";`) with exactly the 9 TESTS cases.
  4. Run DONE, then `bun run lint` and `bun run typecheck`.
- **DONE:** `bun test convex/lib/bounded.test.ts` → `9 pass`, `0 fail`.
- **EVIDENCE:** the `bun test` summary plus the `bun run lint` and `bun run typecheck` exit codes, pasted into the PR.
- **DO NOT:** change any existing query to call the helper (later tickets do); measure bytes with `string.length` or `JSON.stringify(x).length` alone; sort or skip rows; use `ConvexError` (new modules throw plain `Error`, CONVENTIONS §8); touch `convex/schema.ts`, `convex/auth*`, `.github/**`, `.env*`.
- **REPORT:** AGENTS.md format — `status / ticket: TFV2-0001 / evidence: <DONE command> -> <summary> / changed: convex/lib/bounded.ts, convex/lib/bounded.test.ts / unknowns / notes for ticket sync`; list STEPS 1–4 each with its evidence.
- **SPEC:**
  ```ts
  export type BoundedOptions = { maxRows: number; maxBytes: number };
  export type BoundedResult<T> = { rows: T[]; truncated: boolean };
  /** UTF-8 byte length of the row's JSON form: new TextEncoder().encode(JSON.stringify(row)).length. */
  export function rowUtf8Bytes(row: unknown): number;
  export function boundedQuery<T>(rows: readonly T[], opts: BoundedOptions): BoundedResult<T>;
  ```
  - Validation first: `opts.maxRows` must satisfy `Number.isSafeInteger(x) && x >= 0`, else `throw new Error("maxRows must be a non-negative integer")`; then the same for `opts.maxBytes` with `"maxBytes must be a non-negative integer"`.
  - Algorithm: walk `rows` in input order with `kept: T[] = []` and `used = 0`. For each row: if `kept.length === opts.maxRows` → stop with `truncated: true`; let `b = rowUtf8Bytes(row)`; if `used + b > opts.maxBytes` → stop with `truncated: true`; else push the row (same reference) and add `b`. Reaching the end of `rows` returns `truncated: false`. A row that does not fit ends the walk; later smaller rows are never taken.
  - `rowUtf8Bytes(undefined)` treats `JSON.stringify(undefined)` (which is `undefined`) as `"null"` → 4 bytes.
  - The input array is never mutated. No user-facing copy (callers own copy). No database access.
- **TESTS:** (`convex/lib/bounded.test.ts`; `const row = (n: number) => ({ s: "a".repeat(n - 8) })` is a row whose JSON is exactly `n` UTF-8 bytes, because `{"s":""}` is 8 bytes)
  1. Given `rows = []`, `{ maxRows: 10, maxBytes: 1_000 }` / When `boundedQuery` runs / Then it returns `{ rows: [], truncated: false }`.
  2. Given 10 rows `row(100)` and `{ maxRows: 5, maxBytes: 1_000_000 }` / Then `rows.length === 5`, `truncated === true`, and `rows[0]` is the same object as the input's first row (`toBe`).
  3. Given 3 rows `row(100)` and `{ maxRows: 10, maxBytes: 250 }` / Then `rows.length === 2` and `truncated === true`.
  4. Given 2 rows `row(100)` and `{ maxRows: 10, maxBytes: 200 }` / Then `rows.length === 2` and `truncated === false` (an exact fit is not truncated).
  5. Given `[{ s: "שלום" }]` (UTF-16 JSON length 14, UTF-8 length 16) / When `maxBytes` is 15 / Then `{ rows: [], truncated: true }`; when `maxBytes` is 16 / Then one row and `truncated === false`; and `rowUtf8Bytes({ s: "שלום" }) === 16`.
  6. Given `{ maxRows: 0, maxBytes: 100 }` / When rows are `[row(10)]` / Then `{ rows: [], truncated: true }`; when rows are `[]` / Then `{ rows: [], truncated: false }`.
  7. Given `maxRows: -1` and, separately, `maxRows: 1.5` / Then each call throws `"maxRows must be a non-negative integer"`.
  8. Given `maxBytes: Number.NaN` and, separately, `maxBytes: Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY` / Then each call throws `"maxBytes must be a non-negative integer"`.
  9. Given `rows = [3, 1, 2]` and `{ maxRows: 10, maxBytes: 100 }` / Then `rows` returned equals `[3, 1, 2]` (input order) and the input array still equals `[3, 1, 2]`.
- **NUMBERS:** 9 of 9 cases pass (exact). Byte counts are exact UTF-8 lengths (TESTS 5; CONVENTIONS §7 H). The helper holds no default budget: each caller names its own exported constant (CONVENTIONS §16). Latency: n/a (pure, in-memory, O(n)).
- **GATES:** 1 Build/typecheck/lint · 2 own TESTS green · 3 NUMBERS in range · 4 Google style formatting/naming · 5 secret + forbidden-tech scan · 6 scope guard · 7 config guard · 8 never weaken/skip/lower/delete a check · 9 Jev judge (typesafe/jev-1.13): instruction-following, formatting, naming, clean code each >= 0.85; a massive violation fails · 10 Process check: REPORT lists every STEP and DONE item with evidence; a missing item fails.
- **OPEN:** none.

- **SPEC:**
  ```ts
  import type { AiCallOptions, AiResult } from "./ai_router";
  export const MOCK_MODEL_ID = "mock-model";
  export const MOCK_FALLBACK_REPLY = "Done.";
  export type MockModel = ((opts: AiCallOptions) => Promise<AiResult>) & { readonly calls: readonly AiCallOptions[] };
  export function mockModel(queue: readonly string[]): MockModel;
  ```
  - `mockModel` copies `queue` when called (later changes to the caller's array have no effect).
  - Each call validates `opts.messages`: it must be an array with length ≥ 1 whose every item is an object with `role` in `"system" | "user" | "assistant"` and `typeof content === "string"`. Otherwise the returned promise rejects with `new Error("Bad messages for the mock model")` and the call is not recorded.
  - A valid call is pushed to `calls` (the same `opts` object), then resolves to `{ tier: opts.tier, requestedTier: opts.tier, model: MOCK_MODEL_ID, content, usage: { promptTokens: 0, completionTokens: 0, totalTokens: 0 }, escalated: false }`, where `content` is the next queued reply in order, or `MOCK_FALLBACK_REPLY` once the queue is empty.
  - No user-facing copy; no network, env or database access.
- **TESTS:** (`convex/lib/mockModel.test.ts`; `const msgs = [{ role: "user" as const, content: "hi" }]`)
  1. Given `mockModel(["First", "Second"])` / When called twice with `{ tier: "balanced", messages: msgs }` / Then the results' `content` are `"First"` then `"Second"`.
  2. Given `mockModel([])` / When called once / Then `content === "Done."` and `calls.length === 1`.
  3. Given three queued replies and four calls / Then the fourth `content` is `"Done."`.
  4. Given one call with `opts = { tier: "fast", messages: msgs, maxTokens: 50 }` / Then `calls[0]` is that same object (`toBe`).
  5. Given `mockModel(["x"])` called with tier `"deep"` / Then the result `toEqual`s `{ tier: "deep", requestedTier: "deep", model: "mock-model", content: "x", usage: { promptTokens: 0, completionTokens: 0, totalTokens: 0 }, escalated: false }`.
  6. Given `messages: [{ role: "tool", content: "x" }]` (cast through `unknown`) / Then the promise rejects with `"Bad messages for the mock model"` and `calls.length === 0`.
  7. Given `messages: []` / Then it rejects with `"Bad messages for the mock model"`.
  8. Given `messages: [{ role: "user", content: 5 }]` (cast) / Then it rejects with `"Bad messages for the mock model"`.
  9. Given `globalThis.fetch` replaced by a `mock()` that throws, restored in `afterEach` / When the mock model is called / Then the fetch mock was called 0 times.
  10. Given `const q = ["a"]; const m = mockModel(q); q.push("b");` / When `m` is called twice / Then the contents are `"a"` then `"Done."`; and the file contains `const asSeam: typeof callLLM = mockModel([]);` (with `import type { callLLM } from "./ai_router"`), which `bun run typecheck` compiles.
- **NUMBERS:** 10 of 10 cases pass (exact); 0 network calls (TESTS 9). Latency: n/a (in-memory). No industry number applies.

  2. Create `convex/lib/shameWords.ts` exactly as SPEC. No imports.
  3. Create `convex/lib/shameWords.test.ts` with exactly the 12 TESTS cases.
  4. Run DONE, then `bun run lint` and `bun run typecheck`.
- **DONE:** `bun test convex/lib/shameWords.test.ts` → `12 pass`, `0 fail`.
- **EVIDENCE:** the `bun test` summary plus lint/typecheck exit codes, pasted into the PR.
- **DO NOT:** add, remove or reword a term (the list is CONVENTIONS §12's, exactly); return or log the input text; wire the check into any caller (later tickets); touch `convex/schema.ts`, `convex/auth*`, `.github/**`, `.env*`.
- **REPORT:** AGENTS.md format — `status / ticket: TFV2-0003 / evidence / changed: convex/lib/shameWords.ts, convex/lib/shameWords.test.ts / unknowns / notes for ticket sync`; list STEPS 1–4 each with its evidence.
- **SPEC:**
  ```ts
  export const SHAME_TERMS_EN: readonly string[] = ["failed", "overdue", "lazy", "must", "should have", "streak lost", "you never"];
  export const SHAME_TERMS_HE: readonly string[] = ["נכשל", "איחרת", "עצלן", "חייב", "היית צריך"];
  export type ShameCheck = { found: boolean; matches: string[] };
  export function containsShame(text: string): ShameCheck;
  ```
  - Both arrays are `Object.freeze`d.
  - EN matching: for each term build once, at module load, `new RegExp(\`(?<![\\p{L}\\p{N}])${term.split(" ").join("\\s+")}(?![\\p{L}\\p{N}])\`, "iu")` — case-insensitive, whole word (no letter or digit on either side), any run of whitespace between the words of a phrase.
  - HE matching: plain substring (`text.includes(term)`), so prefixed and inflected forms ("ונכשלתי") are flagged; over-flagging is allowed, under-flagging is not.
  - `matches` lists the canonical terms that matched (never the input text), each once, in order: every EN term in `SHAME_TERMS_EN` order, then every HE term in `SHAME_TERMS_HE` order. `found === matches.length > 0`. The input is not modified. No user-facing copy.
- **TESTS:**
  1. Given `"You failed to finish it."` / Then `{ found: true, matches: ["failed"] }`.
  2. Given `"The task is overdue by a day."` / Then `matches` equals `["overdue"]`.
  3. Given `"Must do the dishes"` / Then `matches` equals `["must"]` (case-insensitive).
  4. Given `"Pass the mustard"` / Then `{ found: false, matches: [] }` (whole word).
  5. Given `"I should   have called"` (three spaces) / Then `matches` equals `["should have"]`.
  6. Given `"You never call"` / Then `matches` equals `["you never"]`.
  7. Given `"איחרת עם המשימה."` / Then `matches` equals `["איחרת"]`.
  8. Given `"ונכשלתי שוב"` / Then `matches` equals `["נכשל"]` (substring for Hebrew).
  9. Given `"Write the plan for Monday."` / Then `{ found: false, matches: [] }`.
  10. Given `"failed and failed again"` / Then `matches` equals `["failed"]` (deduplicated).
  11. Given `"You must, it is overdue"` / Then `matches` equals `["overdue", "must"]` (canonical order, not text order).
  12. Given each term `t` of `SHAME_TERMS_EN` and `SHAME_TERMS_HE` in a loop / When `containsShame(t)` runs / Then `matches` contains `t` (recall 100%); and `containsShame("")` is `{ found: false, matches: [] }`.
- **NUMBERS:** recall on the canonical list = 100% (TESTS 12; source: PRD §13 + CONVENTIONS §12). Precision: not a gate (over-flagging allowed by design). 12 of 12 cases pass. Latency: n/a (pure).
- **GATES:** 1 Build/typecheck/lint · 2 own TESTS green · 3 NUMBERS in range · 4 Google style formatting/naming · 5 secret + forbidden-tech scan · 6 scope guard · 7 config guard · 8 never weaken/skip/lower/delete a check · 9 Jev judge (typesafe/jev-1.13): instruction-following, formatting, naming, clean code each >= 0.85; a massive violation fails · 10 Process check: REPORT lists every STEP and DONE item with evidence; a missing item fails.
- **OPEN:** none.

  ```ts
  export const pageWriteResult = v.object({
    operationId: v.id("pageOperations"),
    revision: v.number(),
    result: v.union(v.literal("applied"), v.literal("noop")),
    undoUntilMs: v.union(v.number(), v.null()),
  });
  export type PageWriteResult = { operationId: Id<"pageOperations">; revision: number; result: "applied" | "noop"; undoUntilMs: number | null };

  export const save = mutation({
    args: { noteId: v.id("notes"), expectedRevision: v.number(), body: v.string(), requestId: v.string() },
    returns: pageWriteResult,
    handler: async (ctx: MutationCtx, args: { noteId: Id<"notes">; expectedRevision: number; body: string; requestId: string }): Promise<PageWriteResult> => { … },
  });

  // module-private helpers (not exported)
  const LEDGER_ERROR_MESSAGES: Partial<Record<PageLedgerErrorCode, string>> = {
    invalid_request_id: "Invalid request id",
    request_id_expired: "Invalid request id",
    request_id_in_future: "Invalid request id",
    request_id_reused: "Request id already used",
    revision_mismatch: "Revision conflict",
    body_too_large_utf16: "Page body is too long",
    body_too_large_utf8: "Page body is too long",
  };
  function unwrap<T>(result: PageLedgerResult<T>): T; // ok → value; else throw new Error(LEDGER_ERROR_MESSAGES[code] ?? `Page write rejected: ${code}`)
  async function loadOwnedLiveNote(ctx: MutationCtx, userId: Id<"users">, noteId: Id<"notes">): Promise<Doc<"notes">>; // missing, other owner or deletedAt set → throw new Error("Note not found")
  async function admitPageRequest(ctx: MutationCtx, input: { userId: Id<"users">; noteId: Id<"notes">; requestId: string; requestDigest: string; nowMs: number }): Promise<Doc<"pageOperations"> | null>;
  function toWriteResult(op: Doc<"pageOperations">): PageWriteResult; // { operationId: op._id, revision: op.resultRevision, result: op.result, undoUntilMs: op.undoUntilMs ?? null }
  async function commitPageChange(ctx: MutationCtx, input: { userId: Id<"users">; note: Doc<"notes">; requestId: string; requestDigest: string; kind: "save" | "patch_block"; plan: BodyChangePlan; nowMs: number }): Promise<PageWriteResult>;
  ```
  - `admitPageRequest`: `matches = await ctx.db.query("pageOperations").withIndex("by_userId_requestId", (q) => q.eq("userId", userId).eq("requestId", requestId)).take(2)`; `admission = unwrap(decideRequestAdmission({ nowMs, userId, noteId, requestId, requestDigest, matches }))`; returns `matches[0]` when `admission.decision === "replay"`, else `null`.
  - `commitPageChange`: `facts = unwrap(buildOperationFacts({ userId, noteId: note._id, requestId, requestDigest, kind, source: "ui", change: plan.facts, nowMs }))`; `operationId = await ctx.db.insert("pageOperations", facts)`; when `plan.facts.result === "applied"`: `operation = await ctx.db.get(operationId)`, `payload = unwrap(buildPayloadFacts({ operation, splices: plan.splices, nowMs }))`, `await ctx.db.insert("pageOperationPayloads", payload)`, `await ctx.db.patch(note._id, { body: plan.resultBody, revision: plan.facts.resultRevision, updatedAt: nowMs })`. A `noop` writes only the receipt and leaves the note untouched. Returns `toWriteResult` of the inserted operation.
  - `save` handler order (fixed; the order decides which error wins): 1) `user = await requireUser(ctx)`; 2) `note = await loadOwnedLiveNote(ctx, user._id, args.noteId)`; 3) `requestDigest = unwrap(await computePageRequestDigest({ kind: "save", noteId: args.noteId, expectedRevision: args.expectedRevision, body: args.body }))`; 4) `nowMs = Date.now()`; `replay = await admitPageRequest(…)`; if `replay` return `toWriteResult(replay)`; 5) `unwrap(checkExpectedRevision(note.revision, args.expectedRevision))`; 6) `plan = unwrap(await planBodyChange({ before: note.body, after: args.body, noteRevision: note.revision }))`; 7) `return commitPageChange(ctx, { userId: user._id, note, requestId: args.requestId, requestDigest, kind: "save", plan, nowMs })`.
  - Budgets (code truth, `PAGE_LEDGER_LIMITS`): a written body is ≤ 1,048,576 UTF-16 units **and** ≤ 131,072 UTF-8 bytes (128 KiB). A byte-identical body is a `noop` (revision unchanged, `undoUntilMs: null`). A missing `notes.revision` counts as 0.
  - Errors (exact message · trigger · test):
    | message | trigger | TESTS |
    |---|---|---|
    | `Not authenticated` | no identity | 5 |
    | `Note not found` | note owned by another user | 6 |
    | `Note not found` | note has `deletedAt` | 7 |
    | `Revision conflict` | `expectedRevision` ≠ stored revision | 8 |
    | `Page body is too long` | body of 131,073 ASCII bytes | 9 |
    | `Invalid request id` | `requestId` not `req_` + ULID | 10 |
    | `Invalid request id` | ULID time older than 24 h | 11 |
    | `Request id already used` | same `requestId`, different body | 12 |
    | `Page write rejected: <code>` | any other ledger failure; tested with `malformed_text` | 13 |
  - Copy: backend errors are English only (CONVENTIONS §11); the screen maps them.
- **TESTS:** (`describe("notes.save")` in `convex/notes.test.ts`; every case seeds `const ctx = ledgerCtx("users:1", ["users:2"])` and `const noteId = await ctx.db.insert("notes", { userId: "users:1", title: "P", body: "Hello", pinned: false, periodType: "none", createdAt: 1, updatedAt: 1 })`; `reqId` is
  ```ts
  const CROCKFORD = "0123456789ABCDEFGHJKMNPQRSTVWXYZ";
  function reqId(ms = Date.now(), tail = "0000000000000000"): string {
    let t = ms; let time = "";
    for (let i = 0; i < 10; i += 1) { time = CROCKFORD[t % 32] + time; t = Math.floor(t / 32); }
    return `req_${time}${tail}`;
  }
  ```
  and a second distinct id uses `tail = "0000000000000001"`.)
  1. Given the note / When `save({ noteId, expectedRevision: 0, body: "Hello world", requestId: reqId() })` runs / Then the result is `{ result: "applied", revision: 1, operationId, undoUntilMs }` with `undoUntilMs === op.appliedAtMs + 300_000`; the note has `body "Hello world"`, `revision 1`, `updatedAt === op.appliedAtMs`; exactly one `pageOperations` row with `kind "save"`, `source "ui"`, `result "applied"`, `baseRevision 0`, `resultRevision 1`; exactly one `pageOperationPayloads` row whose `payload` equals `{ state: "available", splices: [{ startUtf16: 5, removedText: "", insertedText: " world" }] }`.
  2. Given that save, then `save({ noteId, expectedRevision: 1, body: "Hello there", requestId: reqId(Date.now(), "0000000000000001") })` / Then the second result has `revision 2` and the note's `revision` is 2.
  3. Given `save({ noteId, expectedRevision: 0, body: "Hello", requestId: reqId() })` (unchanged body) / Then `{ result: "noop", revision: 0, undoUntilMs: null }`, the note's `updatedAt` is still 1 and `revision` still absent, one `pageOperations` row with `result "noop"`, zero `pageOperationPayloads` rows.
  4. Given the same `save` args (same `requestId`) run twice / Then both results are deep-equal, there is exactly one `pageOperations` row and the note's `revision` is 1.
  5. Given `makeSignedOutCtx()` / When `save` runs / Then it rejects with `"Not authenticated"`.
  6. Given a note seeded with `userId: "users:2"` / When user 1 saves it / Then it rejects with `"Note not found"`, its body is unchanged and there are 0 `pageOperations` rows.
  7. Given the user's note patched with `deletedAt: 5` / Then `save` rejects with `"Note not found"`.
  8. Given the note patched to `revision: 3` / When `save` runs with `expectedRevision: 2` / Then it rejects with `"Revision conflict"` and there are 0 `pageOperations` rows.
  9. Given `body: "a".repeat(131_073)` / Then it rejects with `"Page body is too long"` and the note body is still `"Hello"`.
  10. Given `requestId: "req_nope"` / Then it rejects with `"Invalid request id"`.
  11. Given `requestId: reqId(Date.now() - 25 * 3_600_000)` / Then it rejects with `"Invalid request id"`.
  12. Given a first successful save with `reqId()`, then a second call with the same `requestId` and `body: "Other"` / Then the second rejects with `"Request id already used"` and the body is still `"Hello world"`.
  13. Given `body: "\uD800"` (a lone surrogate) / Then it rejects with `"Page write rejected: malformed_text"`.
- **NUMBERS:** body budget ≤ 131,072 UTF-8 bytes and ≤ 1,048,576 UTF-16 units (`PAGE_LEDGER_LIMITS`, code truth; TESTS 9); Undo window = 300,000 ms (`PAGE_LEDGER_TIMING.undoWindowMs`, PRD F-131; TESTS 1); revision advances by exactly 1 per applied save (TESTS 1–2).  
  ```ts
  export const patchBlock = mutation({
    args: {
      noteId: v.id("notes"),
      expectedRevision: v.number(),
      blockId: v.string(),
      patch: v.record(v.string(), v.union(v.string(), v.number(), v.boolean(), v.null())),
      requestId: v.string(),
    },
    returns: pageWriteResult,
    handler: async (ctx: MutationCtx, args: { noteId: Id<"notes">; expectedRevision: number; blockId: string; patch: Record<string, string | number | boolean | null>; requestId: string }): Promise<PageWriteResult> => { … },
  });
  /** One block's source in the codec's fence form, keeping the original line ending. */
  function taskBlockSource(block: TempoBlock, originalSource: string): string {
    const eol = /(?:\r\n|\r|\n)$/.exec(originalSource)?.[0] ?? "";
    return `\`\`\`json tempo\n${JSON.stringify(block)}\n\`\`\`${eol}`;
  }
  ```
  - Handler order: 1) `requireUser`; 2) `loadOwnedLiveNote`; 3) `requestDigest = unwrap(await computePageRequestDigest({ kind: "patch_block", noteId, expectedRevision, blockId, patch }))` — this validates the patch: unknown key → `patch_not_allowed`, value that fails its `taskDataSchema` field → `patch_value_invalid`, empty patch → `invalid_shape`; 4) `nowMs`, `admitPageRequest` → replay returns early; 5) `unwrap(checkExpectedRevision(note.revision, expectedRevision))`; 6) `segment = parseTempoBlocks(note.body).find((s) => s.kind === "valid" && s.block.id === blockId)`; none → `throw new Error("Block not found")`; `segment.block.type !== "task"` → `throw new Error("Block is not a task")`; 7) `next = { ...segment.block, data: { ...segment.block.data, ...patch } }`, `source = taskBlockSource(next, segment.source)`; `splices = source === segment.source ? [] : [{ startUtf16: segment.start, removedText: segment.source, insertedText: source }]`; 8) `plan = unwrap(await planSpliceChange({ before: note.body, splices, noteRevision: note.revision }))`; 9) `return commitPageChange(ctx, { …, kind: "patch_block", plan, nowMs })`.
  - Everything before `segment.start` and after `segment.end` stays byte-identical. A patch that changes nothing is a `noop` receipt.
  - Errors (exact message · trigger · test):
    | message | trigger | TESTS |
    |---|---|---|
    | `Not authenticated` | no identity | 4 |
    | `Note not found` | note owned by another user | 5 |
    | `Block not found` | no valid block has `blockId` | 6 |
    | `Block is not a task` | `blockId` is a `page-meta` block | 7 |
    | `Revision conflict` | stale `expectedRevision` | 8 |
    | `Page write rejected: patch_not_allowed` | patch key `color` | 9 |
    | `Page write rejected: patch_value_invalid` | `durationMin: 0` | 10 |
    | `Request id already used` | same `requestId`, different patch | 11 |
    | `Page body is too long` | patched body over 131,072 UTF-8 bytes | 12 |
- **TESTS:** (`describe("notes.patchBlock")`; fixture helpers as in TFV2-0006: `id(n)`, `fence(json)`, `task(n)` (status `"later"`, `durationMin` 5), `meta(n)`; seed the note body as given per case with `revision` absent)
  1. Given body `"Intro\n" + task(1) + "Outro\n"` / When `patchBlock({ noteId, expectedRevision: 0, blockId: id(1), patch: { status: "done" }, requestId: reqId() })` runs / Then the result is `applied` with `revision 1`; re-parsing the new body gives block `id(1)` with `data.status "done"` and every other data field unchanged; the new body starts with `"Intro\n"` and ends with `"Outro\n"`; the `pageOperations` row has `kind "patch_block"`.
  2. Given body `task(1) + task(2)` / When `id(2)` is patched with `{ title: "New" }` / Then the new body starts with exactly `task(1)` (byte-identical).
  3. Given body `task(1)` / When patched with `{ status: "later" }` (its current value) / Then `{ result: "noop", revision: 0, undoUntilMs: null }` and the body is unchanged.
  4. Given `makeSignedOutCtx()` / Then it rejects with `"Not authenticated"`.
  5. Given the note owned by `"users:2"` / Then it rejects with `"Note not found"`.
  6. Given body `task(1)` and `blockId: id(9)` / Then it rejects with `"Block not found"` and there are 0 `pageOperations` rows.
  7. Given body `meta(1) + task(2)` and `blockId: id(1)` / Then it rejects with `"Block is not a task"`.
  8. Given the note patched to `revision: 2` and `expectedRevision: 1` / Then it rejects with `"Revision conflict"`.
  9. Given `patch: { color: "red" }` / Then it rejects with `"Page write rejected: patch_not_allowed"`.
  10. Given `patch: { durationMin: 0 }` / Then it rejects with `"Page write rejected: patch_value_invalid"`.
  11. Given a successful patch with `reqId()`, then the same `requestId` with `patch: { status: "now" }` / Then the second rejects with `"Request id already used"`.
  12. Given body `task(1) + "a".repeat(131_072 - new TextEncoder().encode(task(1)).length)` (exactly at the budget) and `patch: { title: "x".repeat(400) }` / Then it rejects with `"Page body is too long"` and the body is unchanged.
- **NUMBERS:** untouched bytes outside the block = 100% identical (TESTS 1–2); body budget ≤ 131,072 UTF-8 bytes (`PAGE_LEDGER_LIMITS.maxBodyUtf8Bytes`; TESTS 12). Backend p95 latency: UNKNOWN (no baseline; not a gate).

- **SPEC:**
  ```ts
  export const undo = mutation({
    args: { noteId: v.id("notes"), targetOperationId: v.id("pageOperations"), requestId: v.string() },
    returns: pageWriteResult,
    handler: async (ctx: MutationCtx, args: { noteId: Id<"notes">; targetOperationId: Id<"pageOperations">; requestId: string }): Promise<PageWriteResult> => { … },
  });
  ```
  Handler order:
  1. `user = await requireUser(ctx)`; `note = await loadOwnedLiveNote(ctx, user._id, args.noteId)`.
  2. `target = await ctx.db.get(args.targetOperationId)`; if `!target || target.userId !== user._id || target.noteId !== args.noteId || target.deletedAt !== undefined` → `throw new Error("Change not found")`.
  3. `requestDigest = unwrap(await computePageRequestDigest({ kind: "undo", noteId: args.noteId, targetOperationId: args.targetOperationId }))`; `nowMs = Date.now()`; `replay = await admitPageRequest(…)` → return `toWriteResult(replay)`.
  4. `decision = unwrap(decideUndoRequest({ nowMs, target }))`; if `decision.decision === "already_undone"` → return `toWriteResult((await ctx.db.get(decision.undoOperationId as Id<"pageOperations">))!)` (no write).
  5. `payload = await ctx.db.query("pageOperationPayloads").withIndex("by_userId_operationId", (q) => q.eq("userId", user._id).eq("operationId", target._id)).first()`.
  6. `intervening = await ctx.db.query("pageOperations").withIndex("by_userId_noteId_affectsBody_resultRevision", (q) => q.eq("userId", user._id).eq("noteId", args.noteId).eq("affectsBody", true).gte("resultRevision", target.resultRevision + 1)).take(PAGE_LEDGER_LIMITS.maxInterveningRevisions + 1)`.
  7. `plan = unwrap(await planUndo({ nowMs, userId: user._id, noteId: args.noteId, noteRevision: note.revision, currentBody: note.body, target: payload ? { operation: target, payload } : { operation: target }, intervening }))`.
  8. `facts = unwrap(buildOperationFacts({ userId: user._id, noteId: args.noteId, requestId: args.requestId, requestDigest, kind: "undo", source: "ui", change: plan.facts, nowMs, undoOfOperationId: target._id }))`; `undoId = await ctx.db.insert("pageOperations", facts)`.
  9. `marked = unwrap(markOperationUndone({ target, undoOperationId: undoId, nowMs }))`; `await ctx.db.patch(target._id, { undoneAtMs: marked.undoneAtMs, undoneByOperationId: marked.undoneByOperationId, updatedAt: marked.updatedAt })`.
  10. `await ctx.db.patch(args.noteId, { body: plan.candidateBody, revision: plan.facts.resultRevision, updatedAt: nowMs })`; `await rebuildNoteBlocks(ctx, user._id, args.noteId, plan.candidateBody, nowMs)`.
  11. Return `toWriteResult` of the undo row (an `undo` receipt has no window of its own, so `undoUntilMs: null`).
  Errors (exact message · trigger · test):
  | message | trigger | TESTS |
  |---|---|---|
  | `Not authenticated` | no identity | 7 |
  | `Note not found` | note owned by another user | 8 |
  | `Change not found` | target belongs to another note of the same user | 9 |
  | `Undo window has passed` | `now >= undoUntilMs` | 4 |
  | `Undo conflicts with a later edit` | a later edit overlaps the target's inserted text | 3 |
  | `Page write rejected: undo_not_undoable` | target is a `noop` receipt | 10 |
- **TESTS:** (`describe("notes.undo")`; seed as in TFV2-0007a with body `"Hello"`; `saveAs(body, expectedRevision, tail)` calls `save` with `reqId(Date.now(), tail)`)
  1. Given a save `"Hello"` → `"Hello world"` (operation T) / When `undo({ noteId, targetOperationId: T, requestId: reqId(Date.now(), "0000000000000009") })` runs / Then the note body is `"Hello"` and `revision 2`; the result has `revision 2`, `result "applied"`, `undoUntilMs null`; the new `pageOperations` row has `kind "undo"` and `undoOfOperationId T`; row T has `undoneByOperationId` equal to the new id and a numeric `undoneAtMs`.
  2. Given saves `"A\nB"` (seeded body) → `"A\nB\nC"` (T) → `"Z\nB\nC"` / When T is undone / Then the body is `"Z\nB"` (the later edit survives) and `revision 3`.
  3. Given saves `"Hello"` → `"Hello world"` (T) → `"Hello there"` / When T is undone / Then it rejects with `"Undo conflicts with a later edit"` and the body is still `"Hello there"`.
  4. Given a save at time `t0` (T) and `setSystemTime(new Date(t0 + 300_000))` / When T is undone / Then it rejects with `"Undo window has passed"`.
  5. Given T undone once / When `undo` runs again with a different `requestId` / Then it returns the first undo's `operationId`, the body and `revision` are unchanged, and there is exactly one `kind "undo"` row.
  6. Given `undo` run twice with the same `requestId` / Then both results are deep-equal and there is exactly one `kind "undo"` row.
  7. Given `makeSignedOutCtx()` / Then `undo` rejects with `"Not authenticated"`.
  8. Given a note of `"users:2"` / When user 1 calls `undo` on it / Then it rejects with `"Note not found"`.
  9. Given T on note 1 and a second note 2 of the same user / When `undo({ noteId: note2, targetOperationId: T, … })` runs / Then it rejects with `"Change not found"`.
  10. Given a `noop` save receipt N (body unchanged) / When N is undone / Then it rejects with `"Page write rejected: undo_not_undoable"`.
  11. Given a save that appends `task(1)` (T) / When T is undone / Then the page has 0 `noteBlocks` rows.
- **NUMBERS:** Undo window 300,000 ms, half-open (`PAGE_LEDGER_TIMING.undoWindowMs`, PRD F-131; TESTS 4); intervening revisions read ≤ 257 (`PAGE_LEDGER_LIMITS.maxInterveningRevisions` 256 + 1; bounded read). Backend p95 latency: UNKNOWN (no baseline; not a gate).

- **SPEC:**
  ```ts
  /** Gendered second-person forms CONVENTIONS §12 forbids in Hebrew UI copy (feminine, then masculine). */
  export const GENDERED_HE_FORMS: readonly string[] = Object.freeze([
    "לחצי", "תלחצי", "בחרי", "תבחרי", "הקלידי", "כתבי", "תכתבי", "נסי", "תנסי", "שמרי", "הוסיפי", "תוסיפי",
    "בקשי", "העתיקי", "תרשמי", "תחזרי", "כשתחזרי", "תוכלי", "תרצי", "מוכנה", "את צריכה",
    "תלחץ", "תבחר", "תכתוב", "תנסה", "תוסיף", "תחזור", "כשתחזור", "תוכל", "תרצה", "אתה", "מוכן/ה",
  ]);
  /** Every listed form found as a whole word (no Hebrew letter immediately before or after), deduplicated, in list order. */
  export function findGenderedHebrew(text: string): string[];
  ```
  Matching: for each form `f`, `new RegExp(\`(?<![\\u05D0-\\u05EA])${escapeRegExp(f)}(?![\\u05D0-\\u05EA])\`, "u")` where `escapeRegExp` escapes `/` and other regex characters; forms are compiled once at module load. Pure; no errors thrown; no user-facing copy.
- **TESTS:**

  ```tsx
  // apps/web/app/e2e/components/layout.tsx (server component)
  import { type ReactNode, Suspense } from "react";
  import { HarnessFrame } from "@/lib/e2e/HarnessFrame";
  export default function ComponentHarnessLayout({ children }: { children: ReactNode }): JSX.Element {
    return <Suspense fallback={null}><HarnessFrame>{children}</HarnessFrame></Suspense>;
  }

  // apps/web/lib/e2e/HarnessFrame.tsx
  "use client";
  import { notFound, useSearchParams } from "next/navigation";
  import type { ReactNode } from "react";
  import { LocaleProvider } from "@/components/providers/LocaleProvider";
  import { dirFor, resolveLang } from "@/lib/i18n";
  import { isE2EBypass } from "./e2eState";
  export type HarnessTheme = "light" | "dark";
  export function HarnessFrame({ children }: { children: ReactNode }): JSX.Element {
    if (!isE2EBypass({ NODE_ENV: process.env.NODE_ENV, NEXT_PUBLIC_TEMPO_E2E_AUTH_BYPASS: process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_TEMPO_E2E_AUTH_BYPASS })) notFound();
    const params = useSearchParams();
    const lang = resolveLang(params.get("lang"), null);
    const theme: HarnessTheme = params.get("theme") === "dark" ? "dark" : "light";
    return (
      <LocaleProvider>
        <div data-testid="component-harness" lang={lang} dir={dirFor(lang)} data-theme={theme}>{children}</div>
      </LocaleProvider>
    );
  }
  ```
  `LocaleProvider` also sets `<html lang dir>` from `?lang=` on mount, so `expectDir` (which reads `<html>`) agrees with the frame. No user-facing copy; the frame has no states of its own (component states live in each component's page).
- **TESTS:** (`test.skip(!!process.env.PLAYWRIGHT_BASE_URL, "local webServer only");`)
  1–2. For each viewport in `VIEWPORTS`: Given `/e2e/components` / Then `[data-testid="component-harness"]` contains `[data-testid="component-harness-index"]`, and has `lang="en"`, `dir="ltr"`, `data-theme="light"`.
  3. Given `/e2e/components?lang=he` / Then the frame has `lang="he"` and `dir="rtl"`, and `expectDir(page, "he")` passes.
  4. Given `/e2e/components?theme=dark` / Then the frame has `data-theme="dark"`.
  5. Given `/e2e/components?lang=fr&theme=neon` / Then the frame has `lang="en"`, `dir="ltr"`, `data-theme="light"` (invalid values fall back).
- **NUMBERS:** 5 of 5 pass. No UI number applies (developer frame).

  ```tsx
  // apps/web/components/auth/EmailField.tsx ("use client")
  export const EMAIL_PATTERN = /^[^\s@]+@[^\s@]+\.[^\s@]+$/;
  export const EMAIL_PLACEHOLDER = "name@example.com";
  export function isValidEmail(value: string): boolean { return EMAIL_PATTERN.test(value.trim()); }
  export type EmailFieldProps = {
    id: string;                          // input id; help id = `${id}-help`, error id = `${id}-error`
    value: string;
    onChange: (value: string) => void;   // called with event.target.value on every input event
    help?: string;                       // screen-specific helper line (EN/HE given by the screen)
    invalid?: boolean;                   // true → aria-invalid="true" + error line
    disabled?: boolean;
  };
  export function EmailField(props: EmailFieldProps): JSX.Element;
  ```

"true" : undefined} aria-describedby={describedBy} onChange={(e) => onChange(e.target.value)} />` where `describedBy` joins, in order, `${id}-help` (when `help`) and `${id}-error` (when `invalid`) with one space, or is `undefined` when both are absent; `{help && <p className="tp-help" id={`${id}-help`}>{help}</p>}`; `{invalid && <p className="tp-error-text" id={`${id}-error`}><TpIcon name="alert" size="sm" /><span>{before}<span className="tp-ltr">{EMAIL_PLACEHOLDER}</span>{after}</span></p>}` where `before`/`after` are `copy.error` split on `{example}`.

  - `error` EN: "Enter your email, like {example}" / HE: "לכתוב כתובת מייל, כמו {example}"
  - placeholder (not translated, `EMAIL_PLACEHOLDER`): "name@example.com"

RTL: label, help and error follow the page direction; the input stays `dir="ltr"` (an email address is LTR in Hebrew). Keyboard: label click and Tab focus the input; focus ring is the global `:focus-visible` outline. Screen reader: label via `for`; help and error via `aria-describedby`; invalid via `aria-invalid`. Code truth today: `SignUpForm` wraps `SignInForm flow="sign-up"`, so sign-up sends the same magic link as sign-in (`signIn("resend", …)`); a new email becomes a `pending` user (`convex/lib/approval.ts` `initialApprovalStatus`), and the pending person sees `WaitingForApproval` inside `ApprovalGate` after opening the link ("No email is sent when that happens", `approval.next1`). There is no `access.request` mutation, no request table and no Turnstile key. The two flows need different backend, schema and copy, so the screen cannot be specified until Q-04 is answered.
- **GOAL:** `/sign-up` is the v3 sign-up screen for the sign-up policy Amit chooses (Q-04), in EN and HE at 390 and 1280, every state forceable with `?state=`, never revealing whether an email already exists.

Each fixture also fixes what a user action does in forced mode: `"ok"` resolves, `"fail"` rejects with `new Error("fixture")`, `"rate-limit"` rejects with `new Error("TooManyRequests")`, `"hang"` returns `new Promise(() => {})` and never settles, so the spec clicks through without Convex. `forced === "offline"` (any fixture with `online: false`) behaves exactly as `useOnline()` (`@/lib/useOnline`) returning `false`. ### TFV2-0062a — PageEditorView takes backlinks as a prop; NotePage loads them and shows the v3 loading state
- **Stage:** A · **Pass:** 1 · **Depends:** TFV2-0000b, TFV2-0023b, TFV2-0044 · **Folds-in:** none
- **FOR:** Tempo Flow (`Levidavidspublic/tempo-rhythm`); lane per `factory/SLOTS.md`.
- **WHEN:** after TFV2-0000b, TFV2-0023b, TFV2-0044.
- **WHY:** CONVENTIONS §13 (components take their data through props) and §14 (the page-editor screen must render "Linked here" and its loading state from fixtures). Code truth: `apps/web/components/notes/PageEditorView.tsx` reads `useQuery(api.notes.backlinks, …)` inside the component, so a fixture can never show backlinks; its one caller is `NotePage` in `apps/web/components/notes/NotesScreen.tsx` (also mounted by Today's `DailyPage.tsx`), whose loading branch is a plain text line, not the v3 skeleton (`page-editor.html` StateLoading). This ticket moves the backlinks read up into `NotePage` (prop down), draws "Linked here" with the range-1 `Backlinks` block (TFV2-0044, `apps/web/components/blocks/Backlinks.tsx`, props `{ links: readonly BacklinkRow[] | undefined }`, its own loading and empty lines) instead of the inline section, and gives `NotePage` an exported `NoteLoading` view that the screen (TFV2-0062b) reuses, so forced and live loading are the same markup. File set: the component, its single caller (the prop becomes required, so the caller must pass it in the same commit for typecheck to stay green; this takes the slot a Case B stylesheet would use, and no stylesheet is needed: Case A, existing Stage 1 classes), and the harness page. The wiki-link picker (`notes.searchTitles` while the `[[` menu is open; `notes.searchTitles` + `notes.create` when a link is followed) stays inside `PageEditorView`: it runs only on user input, never during a forced render, and moving it would add `useConvex` to `NotePage`, which `NotesScreen.test.tsx` mocks without (Cross-range notes).
- **GOAL:** `PageEditorView` renders "Linked here" with `<Backlinks links={backlinks} />` from a `backlinks` prop and makes no backlinks query, `NotePage` passes `notes.backlinks` to it and shows `NoteLoading` while the page loads, proven by a harness spec of every `PageEditorView` state with the existing notes and Today tests still green.
- **SCOPE:** `apps/web/components/notes/PageEditorView.tsx` · `apps/web/components/notes/NotesScreen.tsx` · `apps/web/app/e2e/components/page-editor-view/page.tsx` · test: `tests/e2e/screens/page-editor-view.spec.ts`.
- **MUTATES:** `apps/web/components/notes/PageEditorView.tsx` (edit) · `apps/web/components/notes/NotesScreen.tsx` (edit: `NotePage` gains one query and passes one prop; new export `NoteLoading` replaces the loading branch) · `apps/web/app/e2e/components/page-editor-view/page.tsx` (new) · `tests/e2e/screens/page-editor-view.spec.ts` (new). No data, no route registration (TFV2-0023a registers `/e2e/components/(.*)`).
- **STEPS:** 1) Code-map check: `grep -n "api.notes.backlinks" apps/web/components/notes/PageEditorView.tsx` (one line today); `grep -n "<PageEditorView" apps/web --include=*.tsx -r` (only `NotesScreen.tsx`); `grep -n "Loading note\|loadingNote" apps/web/components/notes/NotesScreen.test.tsx` (the test expects the text `Loading note.` in the static render; `NoteLoading` keeps it as screen-reader text); `ls apps/web/app/e2e/components` (TFV2-0023b `layout.tsx` present, else `blocked: missing TFV2-0023b`); `grep -n "export function Backlinks\|export type BacklinkRow" apps/web/components/blocks/Backlinks.tsx` (two lines, else `blocked: missing TFV2-0044`). 2) In `PageEditorView.tsx`: rename `type Props` to `export type PageEditorViewProps`, add the `backlinks` prop (type `BacklinkRow` imported from `@/components/blocks/Backlinks`), delete the `useQuery(api.notes.backlinks, …)` line, and replace the whole inline `{backlinks && backlinks.length > 0 ? (<section className="tp-backlinks" …>…</section>) : null}` block with `<Backlinks links={props.backlinks} />` at the same place. 3) In `NotesScreen.tsx` `NotePage`: add `const backlinks = useQuery(api.notes.backlinks, isAuthenticated && profile != null ? { noteId } : "skip");`, pass `backlinks={backlinks}` to `<PageEditorView>`, add `export function NoteLoading()` exactly as in SPEC and return `<NoteLoading />` in the `loadState === "loading" && isAuthenticated` branch. 4) Create the harness page with the seven SPEC states. 5) Create the spec with the CONVENTIONS §22 spec skeleton (harness spec: every test calls `await openHarness(page, "page-editor-view", { lang })`; every locator is scoped to its section, `page.getByTestId("page-editor-view-<state>").locator(…)`) and the 8 TESTS cases. 6) Run DONE.

- **WHY:** PRD §4.1 F-06 (the app proposes one template; one tap accepts); `docs/design/v3/screens/web/new-page.html` (`@states default | empty | loading | error | offline`; one proposed template, a picker of built-in + own templates, "Start a plain note"); CONVENTIONS §9, §14, §17. Code truth (`convex/templates.ts`): `templates.list({ scope?: "all" | "starter" | "mine" })` returns `{ templateId, source: "starter" | "user", name, description?, periodType, sections, body, updatedAt? }[]` (9 starters with English names, then the person's own); `templates.proposeForPage({ periodType, title? })` returns `{ templateId, name, reason } | null` (null for `"none"`); `templates.applyToNote({ templateId, title? })` creates a NEW note from the template and returns its `Id<"notes">`; `notes.create({ title, body, pinned?, periodType? })` makes a blank page. There is no `templates.apply` to an existing page, no `templates.dismissOffer`, no `templates.createFromPage`. So this screen creates the page only when a choice is made, then opens `/notes/<id>`; "Not now" is local (the offer returns on the next visit); "Make this page a template" is left out (the page does not exist yet; templates are made in the Template builder at `/templates/builder`); no Undo toast (the new page has its own Delete with a 5-minute undo). TemplateBlock (TFV2-0047) shows the offer. The route is covered by `"/notes/(.*)"` from TFV2-0062b, and Next.js serves the static `notes/new` segment before `notes/[id]`. The old dependency on TFV2-0062 (unsplit) now points at TFV2-0062b. The state components (TFV2-0120…0123) come later, so the screen writes their tempo.css markup directly.

  ```tsx
  // apps/web/app/(tempo)/notes/new/page.tsx ("use client")
  export type NewPageTemplate = { templateId: string; source: "starter" | "user"; name: string; description?: string; periodType: "daily" | "weekly" | "monthly" | "none"; sections: string[] };
  export type NewPageView = {
    kind: "ready" | "loading" | "error";
    online: boolean;
    type: "daily" | "weekly" | "monthly" | "none";       // from ?type=
    proposal: { templateId: string; name: string } | null;
    templates: NewPageTemplate[];
    create: "ok" | "fail" | "hang";                      // forced-mode outcome of Use / Start a plain note
  };
  export default function Page(): JSX.Element; // <Suspense fallback={null}><NewPageRoute /></Suspense>
  // apps/web/lib/e2e/fixtures/notes-new.ts
  import type { NewPageView } from "@/app/(tempo)/notes/new/page";
  export const FIXTURES: Record<"default" | "empty" | "no-offer" | "loading" | "error" | "offline" | "creating" | "create-error", NewPageView>;
  ```
  Fixtures: `DAILY = { templateId: "starter:daily-page", source: "starter", name: "Daily page", description: "A short outline for one day.", periodType: "daily", sections: ["Today", "Intention", "Schedule", "Notes"] }`, `WEEKLY = { templateId: "starter:weekly-page", source: "starter", name: "Weekly page", description: "A few outcomes and a place for each day.", periodType: "weekly", sections: ["This week", "Focus", "Days", "Carry forward"] }`, `MEETING = { templateId: "starter:meeting-notes", source: "starter", name: "Meeting notes", description: "Agenda, notes and next steps.", periodType: "none", sections: ["Agenda", "Notes", "Next steps"] }`, `OWN = { templateId: "templates:own-1", source: "user", name: "Weekend reset", description: "Kitchen, packing and a short note.", periodType: "none", sections: ["Kitchen", "Packing", "Note"] }`. `default` = `{ kind: "ready", online: true, type: "daily", proposal: { templateId: "starter:daily-page", name: "Daily page" }, templates: [DAILY, WEEKLY, MEETING, OWN], create: "ok" }`; `empty` = `default` with `templates: [DAILY, WEEKLY, MEETING]`; `no-offer` = `default` with `type: "none", proposal: null`; `loading` = `default` with `kind: "loading", templates: []`; `error` = `default` with `kind: "error", templates: [], proposal: null`; `offline` = `default` with `online: false`; `creating` = `default` with `create: "hang"`; `create-error` = `default` with `create: "fail"`.
  `NewPageRoute`: `type` from `useSearchParams().get("type")` (`"daily" | "weekly" | "monthly"`, else `"none"`); `const forced = useE2EState();` Forced mode keeps `view` in state (starting at `FIXTURES[forced in FIXTURES ? forced : "default"]`) and renders `<NewPageForm view={view} actions={fixtureActions} onRetry={() => setView(FIXTURES.default)} />` where `fixtureActions.apply`/`.plain` run the fixture `create` outcome and then `router.push("/notes/note-new")`. Live → `<TemplatesBoundary fallback={(retry) => <LiveNewPage type={type} broken onRetry={retry} />}><LiveNewPage type={type} /></TemplatesBoundary>`. `LiveNewPage({ type, broken?, onRetry? })`: `const { isAuthenticated } = useConvexAuth(); const profile = useQuery(api.users.getProfile, isAuthenticated ? {} : "skip"); const ready = isAuthenticated && profile != null && !broken;` `const templates = useQuery(api.templates.list, ready ? {} : "skip");` `const proposal = useQuery(api.templates.proposeForPage, ready ? { periodType: type } : "skip");` `const online = useOnline();` view = `{ kind: broken ? "error" : templates === undefined || proposal === undefined ? "loading" : "ready", online, type, proposal: proposal ? { templateId: proposal.templateId, name: proposal.name } : null, templates: (templates ?? []).map(({ templateId, source, name, description, periodType, sections }) => ({ templateId, source, name, description, periodType, sections })), create: "ok" }`; actions: `apply(templateId, title)` = `const id = await applyToNote({ templateId, title: title.trim() || undefined }); router.push(\`/notes/${id}\`)`; `plain(title)` = `const id = await createNote({ title: title.trim(), body: "", periodType: type }); router.push(\`/notes/${id}\`)`. (A thrown `templates.list`/`proposeForPage` lands in `TemplatesBoundary`, a module-private `class TemplatesBoundary extends Component<{ fallback: (retry: () => void) => ReactNode; children: ReactNode }, { failed: boolean }>` with `static getDerivedStateFromError() { return { failed: true }; }` that renders `fallback(() => this.setState({ failed: false }))` while failed, else `children`; its fallback re-renders the screen with `broken` so a plain note still works.)
  `NewPageForm({ view, actions, onRetry })` (module-private, shared by forced and live; named `Form` so it never clashes with the exported type `NewPageView`): local state `title` (`""`), `offer` (`"offered" | "dismissed"`), `selected` (`view.proposal?.templateId ?? view.templates[0]?.templateId ?? "plain"`), `busy` (false), `failed` (false). `run(work)`: if `busy || !view.online` return; `busy = true`, `failed = false`; `await work()`; on throw `failed = true`; finally `busy = false` (on success the router has already moved). Markup inside the shell's main: `<div className="tp-page" data-component="PageLayout">` with, in order:
  1. `<header className="tp-pagehead" data-component="PageHeader"><div className="tp-pagehead__text"><h1 className="tp-pagehead__title">{copy.heading}</h1><p className="tp-pagehead__sub">{copy.sub}</p></div></header>`
  2. when `!view.online`: `<div className="tp-notice tp-offline" data-tone="caution" role="status" data-component="StateOffline">` (icon `wifi-off`, text `copy.offline`); when `failed`: `<div className="tp-notice" data-tone="danger" role="alert">` (icon `alert`, `<span className="tp-notice__title">{copy.createErrTitle}</span> <span>{copy.createErrBody}</span>`); when `busy`: `<p className="tp-small tp-muted" role="status">{copy.creating}</p>`.
  3. `<div className="tp-field"><label className="tp-label" htmlFor="np-title">{copy.titleLabel}</label><input className="tp-input" id="np-title" dir="auto" autoComplete="off" value={title} placeholder={copy.titlePh} onChange={(e) => setTitle(e.target.value)} /></div>`
  4. `view.kind === "loading"`: `<div className="tp-state--loading" role="status" data-component="StateLoading"><span className="tp-sr-only">{copy.loading}</span><div className="tp-skeleton tp-skeleton--block" /><div className="tp-skel-list" aria-hidden="true">` + three `<div className="tp-skel-row"><span className="tp-skeleton tp-skel-row__box" /><span className="tp-skel-row__lines"><span className="tp-skeleton tp-skeleton--w{W}" /><span className="tp-skeleton tp-skeleton--sm tp-skeleton--w40" /></span></div>` with W = 60, 80, 40 + `</div></div>`.
  5. `view.kind === "error"`: `<div className="tp-state tp-state--error" role="alert" data-component="StateError"><span className="tp-state__icon"><TpIcon name="refresh" size="lg" /></span><h2 className="tp-state__title">{copy.errorTitle}</h2><p className="tp-state__body">{copy.errorBody}</p><div className="tp-state__actions"><button className="tp-btn tp-btn--secondary" type="button" onClick={onRetry}><TpIcon name="refresh" size="sm" /><span>{copy.retry}</span></button></div></div>`.
  6. `view.kind === "ready" && view.proposal && adds.length > 0` (`adds` = the proposed template's `sections.slice(0, 6)` from `view.templates`): `<TemplateBlock template={{ id: view.proposal.templateId, name: view.proposal.name, adds }} status={offer} pending={busy || !view.online} onUse={({ templateId }) => run(() => actions.apply(templateId, title))} onDismiss={() => setOffer("dismissed")} />`.
  7. `view.kind === "ready"`: `<section className="tp-section" data-component="Section" aria-labelledby="np-pick-h"><div className="tp-section__head"><h2 className="tp-section__title" id="np-pick-h">{view.proposal ? copy.pickOther : copy.pick}</h2><span className="tp-section__count"><span className="tp-num">{view.templates.length + 1}</span> {copy.count}</span></div><div className="tp-template-picker" role="radiogroup" aria-labelledby="np-pick-h" data-component="TemplatePicker">` with one `<button type="button" role="radio" className="tp-template-option" data-template={id} aria-checked={selected === id} tabIndex={selected === id ? 0 : -1} onClick={() => setSelected(id)} onKeyDown={arrows}>` per template, then one for `"plain"`; inside: `<span className="tp-template-option__icon"><TpIcon name={icon} /></span><span className="tp-template-option__name" dir="auto">{name}</span><span className="tp-template-option__desc" dir="auto">{desc}</span><span className="tp-template-option__check"><TpIcon name="check" size="sm" /><span>{copy.chosen}</span></span>` (icon: `periodType` `daily` → `today`, `weekly`/`monthly` → `calendar-grid`, else `template`; plain → `text`; plain name/desc = `copy.plainName`/`copy.plainDesc`; a template without `description` shows no desc span). `arrows`: ArrowDown/ArrowRight → next option, ArrowUp/ArrowLeft → previous (horizontal keys reversed when the computed `direction` is `rtl`), wrapping; the new option is selected and focused. After the picker, when `view.templates.every((t) => t.source === "starter")`: `<p className="tp-help">{copy.emptyHint}</p>`. Then `<div className="tp-toolbar"><button className="tp-btn tp-btn--secondary" type="button" data-action="use-picked" disabled={busy || !view.online} onClick={() => run(() => selected === "plain" ? actions.plain(title) : actions.apply(selected, title))}><TpIcon name="template" size="sm" /><span>{copy.use}</span></button>` + the plain button.
  8. The plain button `<button className="tp-btn tp-btn--ghost" type="button" data-action="plain" disabled={busy || !view.online} onClick={() => run(() => actions.plain(title))}><TpIcon name="text" size="sm" /><span>{copy.plain}</span></button>` sits in that toolbar for `ready`, and alone in a `<div className="tp-toolbar">` after the error block for `error`.

  States: `default`, `empty` (no own templates: hint), `no-offer` (`?type=` none), `loading`, `error`, `offline`, `creating`, `create-error`; success = navigation to `/notes/<id>`. Layout: inside `TempoShell`; picker grid from tempo.css (`auto-fill`, min 180 px cards); toolbar wraps. Keyboard: picker is one Tab stop (roving `tabIndex`), arrows move and choose, Enter/Space on the toolbar buttons; TemplateBlock buttons are native. Screen reader: picker `role="radiogroup"` labelled by its heading, options `role="radio"` with `aria-checked`; notices `role="status"`/`"alert"`. Motion: Stage 1 transitions only.
  Forced mode (CONVENTIONS §14 states the core; written out in full here): `const forced = useE2EState();` (`@/lib/e2e/useE2EState`, TFV2-0000c). When `forced !== null` the page passes `"skip"` to every `useQuery`, never calls a mutation, an action or `signIn`, and renders `FIXTURES[forced in FIXTURES ? forced : "default"]` (an unknown `?state=` value falls back to `default`). Each fixture also fixes what a user action does in forced mode: `"ok"` resolves, `"fail"` rejects with `new Error("fixture")`, `"rate-limit"` rejects with `new Error("TooManyRequests")`, `"hang"` returns `new Promise(() => {})` and never settles, so the spec clicks through without Convex. `forced === "offline"` (any fixture with `online: false`) behaves exactly as `useOnline()` (`@/lib/useOnline`) returning `false`. Here the `create` field uses `"ok"`, `"fail"` and `"hang"`; "Not now" and picking an option only change local state.
  Next.js page exports: an App Router `page.tsx` may export only `default` (plus Next.js route-config names such as `metadata` or `dynamic`; none is used here). A type export is erased at build time, so it is allowed. This page exports exactly `default` and the types `NewPageTemplate` and `NewPageView`; `COPY`, `NewPageRoute`, `LiveNewPage`, `NewPageForm` and `TemplatesBoundary` and every other constant, helper and sub-component stay module-private. The fixtures file imports the type with `import type` and exports only `FIXTURES`.
  State markup: the range-3 state components (TFV2-0120 StateEmpty, TFV2-0121 StateLoading, TFV2-0122 StateError, TFV2-0123 StateOffline, TFV2-0092 Notice, TFV2-0301 LanguageSwitch) come later in the backlog, so no ticket here can depend on them; this screen writes their existing `apps/web/app/tempo.css` markup directly (no new class, no stylesheet) with the same `data-component` value the component carries: `@component StateLoading` (`.tp-state--loading` + `.tp-skel-list` + `.tp-skel-row` + `.tp-skeleton`), `@component StateError` (`.tp-state.tp-state--error`), `@component StateOffline` (`.tp-notice.tp-offline[data-tone=caution]`) and the danger notice `.tp-notice[data-tone=danger]`. The exact markup of each is written out in this SPEC.
  Profile gate (CONVENTIONS §22 `ProfileReady` fact): no `ProfileReady` wrapper: `LiveNewPage` reads `users.getProfile` itself and passes `"skip"` to `templates.list` and `templates.proposeForPage` until `profile` is a row (`ready`), the same rule `ProfileReady` applies. Icons come from `TempoShell`'s mounted `TpIconSprite`; no test asserts an icon.
